labs.name: OpenAI
labs.tagline: The mainstream face of generative AI
labs.description: Founded as a non-profit and now a commercial juggernaut, OpenAI turned ChatGPT into the consumer face of generative AI. The strategy: ship the broadest, most distribution-friendly model line on the planet. GPT-5.x for general chat, the o-series for slow reasoning, GPT-Image and Sora for multimodal. Heavy enterprise push through the Microsoft alliance, but the consumer brand is what carries the company.

models.name: GPT-5.5 Instant
models.blurb: Default ChatGPT model since March 2026. 52.5% fewer hallucinations than 5.4 on high-stakes prompts. Lower verbosity by default, tool-use trained from the start.

models.name: GPT-5.4 Think
models.blurb: The slow-thinking option. Outpaces other reasoning models on AIME 2025 and SWE-bench Verified. Expensive per token, reserve for problems where wrong answers cost real money.

models.name: GPT-Image-2
models.blurb: Best in class for images that need legible text baked into the composition. Sticky for posters, infographics, and any case where letters must render correctly.

labs.name: Anthropic
labs.description: Spun out of OpenAI in 2021 by Dario and Daniela Amodei, Anthropic positions itself as the safety-conscious frontier lab. Claude is the model developers reach for when they want long context, careful reasoning, and an assistant that pushes back when it should. Constitutional AI is the methodology, and the Responsible Scaling Policy is the public commitment. Valuation north of $900B at the latest raise, ARR up 80x year over year.

models.name: Claude Opus 4.7
models.blurb: Anthropic's frontier model. Strongest on extended thinking, tool orchestration, and refusing to hallucinate when uncertain. The model developers describe as 'feels like a senior engineer.'

models.name: Claude Sonnet 4.6
models.blurb: The workhorse. Hits the cost-quality sweet spot for most production use cases. Powers Claude Code, the daily-driver for most Anthropic API customers.

models.name: Claude Haiku 4.5
models.blurb: Sub-second responses. The model to pick when you need 10,000 quick judgements rather than one careful one. Often paired as the auxiliary model alongside Sonnet.

labs.name: Google DeepMind
labs.vibe: Research depth, Search distribution, multimodal native
labs.description: DeepMind, originally a London research lab acquired by Google in 2014, is now the unified AI arm under the Google DeepMind banner. The Gemini family powers Search AI Overviews, Workspace, Android, and the standalone Gemini app. Strategy: lean on the world's biggest distribution moat plus 25 years of accumulated research. Strong multimodal from day one, aggressive on agent products through Gemini Spark.

models.name: Gemini 3.5 Pro
models.blurb: 2M token context is the headline. Genuinely useful for parsing hour-long video, full codebases, or multi-document research synthesis in a single prompt.

models.name: Gemini 3.5 Flash
models.blurb: The price-leader. Decent quality at fractions of frontier-model cost. Powers consumer Gemini app and most Google product surfaces.

models.name: Gemini Spark
models.blurb: Google's autonomous agent model. Trained for tool-use and computer-use trajectories. The bet that the next AI wave is agents, not chatbots.

labs.name: Meta AI
labs.vibe: Open source champion, infrastructure scale, social distribution
labs.description: FAIR became Meta AI, and the Llama series became the open-weights frontier. Strategy is unusual: Mark Zuckerberg's bet is that open models commoditise the layer above the chip, making Meta's app distribution and Reality Labs hardware more valuable. Llama 4 ships as both Maverick and Scout variants, plus quantised editions for edge inference. Available on every cloud, every laptop, every phone.

models.name: Llama 4 Maverick
models.blurb: The flagship open-weights model. 405B mixture-of-experts, weights downloadable, license commercially permissive. The default starting point for serious self-hosters.

models.name: Llama 4 Scout
models.blurb: The smaller sibling. Runs on a single H100 at full precision, on consumer hardware quantised. The model researchers actually run locally.

models.name: Llama 4 Omni
models.blurb: Native multimodal with audio in/out and video in. Built for the Reality Labs hardware roadmap. Real-time conversation latency under 300ms.

labs.name: xAI
labs.description: Elon Musk's frontier lab, with the implicit edge of X (formerly Twitter) as a real-time data feed. Grok has shipped four major versions in under two years. The pitch: a model trained on the live pulse of human conversation, with fewer of the guardrails that make competitors feel hedged. Grok Build 0.1 is xAI's bid for the agentic-coding space, going head to head with Claude Code and Cursor.

models.name: Grok 4
models.blurb: Live X integration means current events without a stale knowledge cutoff. Strongest pure-LLM at math benchmarks at release. Less hedged on political and controversial topics than other frontier models.

models.name: Grok Build 0.1
models.blurb: xAI's coding agent model. Aggressive pricing to undercut Claude Sonnet on a per-token basis. Whether it can actually compete on Sonnet's quality is the open question.

models.name: Grok Vision
models.blurb: Strong on chart and document understanding. Often picked for OCR-heavy workflows where Claude and GPT are overkill.

labs.name: Mistral AI
labs.vibe: European sovereignty play, open + closed hybrid
labs.description: Paris-based, founded by Meta and DeepMind alumni, Mistral represents Europe's bid for AI sovereignty. The strategy is a hybrid: open weights for some models (Mistral, Codestral, Mixtral), commercial APIs for the frontier (Mistral Large). Strong on European languages, structured outputs, and tool-use. Notable for shipping fast and not over-engineering safety theatre.

models.name: Mistral Large 3
models.blurb: Mistral's commercial flagship. Function calling and JSON-mode are reliable at production scale. The European go-to where data residency and language coverage matter.

models.name: Codestral 2
models.blurb: Code-specialised, open weights, very low latency. The default IDE autocomplete model when you self-host.

models.name: Mixtral 8x22B
models.blurb: Mixture-of-experts open-weights model. The sparse-MoE option for self-hosters who want frontier-ish quality without Llama 4's compute requirements.

labs.name: Qwen (Alibaba)
labs.vibe: Open weights, Chinese language strength, aggressive iteration
labs.description: Alibaba's frontier AI lab and the most prolific releaser of open-weights models in 2025-2026. Qwen3 was a step-change in open-source quality, Qwen3.7 caught up on Western benchmarks. The strategy is volume: ship a new variant every six weeks, from 0.5B edge models to 200B+ flagships. Strong on Chinese and English, weaker on niche European languages.

models.name: Qwen3.7 Max
models.blurb: The flagship Qwen model. Closes most of the gap with closed frontier models on English benchmarks. Strong in Chinese language at the top of all leaderboards.

models.name: Qwen3.7 Coder
models.blurb: Code-tuned variant. Aggressive pricing and competitive quality. A common pick to undercut OpenAI on coding workflows.

models.name: Qwen3.7 Omni
models.blurb: Open-weights native multimodal. Audio in/out, video understanding, image generation in one model. The closest open answer to GPT-4o-class capability.

labs.name: DeepSeek
labs.tagline: The lab that proved compute isn't everything
labs.vibe: Compute efficiency, open weights, MoE specialists
labs.description: The lab that shocked Silicon Valley in early 2025 by training a frontier-class model for a tiny fraction of OpenAI's reported cost. DeepSeek's mixture-of-experts architecture became the template much of the open-source world now copies. R-series for reasoning, V-series for general use, all weights downloadable, all licensing permissive.

models.name: DeepSeek R2
models.blurb: Open-weights reasoning model that matches GPT-5.4 Think on math and competitive programming at roughly 1/30th the price. The model researchers benchmark against.

models.name: DeepSeek V3.5
models.blurb: General-purpose flagship. Sparse MoE with 671B total params, 37B active per token. Quality close to Sonnet-class, cost close to Haiku-class. The price-quality outlier of 2026.

models.name: DeepSeek Coder V3
models.blurb: Code-tuned variant of V3. The default open-weights pick for self-hosted coding agents in the open-source community.

labs.name: Cohere
labs.description: Founded by Aidan Gomez, one of the original Transformer paper authors, Cohere bet on enterprise from day one rather than consumer chat. The Command family is built for retrieval-augmented workflows, structured outputs, and on-premise deployment. Strong multilingual coverage. Quiet, profitable, undervalued relative to the noise of its US rivals.

models.name: Command A
models.blurb: Cohere's flagship. Tuned for retrieval-augmented generation from day one. Strong at citing sources from provided context rather than inventing them.

models.name: Command R+
models.blurb: The mid-tier workhorse. Tool-use trained, citation-aware, half the cost of GPT-5.5 Instant for many practical tasks.

models.name: Embed v4
models.blurb: State-of-the-art embedding model with multimodal support. The default pick for serious enterprise vector-search stacks.

labs.name: Perplexity
labs.vibe: AI as search engine, not chat
labs.description: Perplexity reframed AI as a search interface rather than a conversation. The product cites every claim back to a source. The Sonar model family is fine-tuned on top of open-weights bases (Llama, Mistral) specifically for grounded, citation-aware answering. The bet: the future of search is AI that shows its work.

models.name: Sonar Pro
models.blurb: Built for search-native applications. Every claim carries a citation chain back to the underlying web source. The model to pick when you need answers AND receipts.

models.name: Sonar Reasoning
models.blurb: Reasoning variant that searches the web mid-thought. Multi-hop questions answered with reasoning traces and source links throughout.

labs.name: Perceptron
labs.tagline: Spatial intelligence for the physical world
labs.description: A newer entrant focused on spatial intelligence — models that understand the physical world rather than just text. Perceptron Mk1 (Mark One) is their flagship vision-reasoning model, trained on multimodal data with a heavy weighting toward 3D scene understanding, robotics datasets, and embodied trajectories. The pitch: AI for the layer below chatbots.

models.name: Perceptron Mk1
models.blurb: Perceptron's highest-quality vision-reasoning model. Strong at spatial relationships, depth estimation from single images, and converting visual scenes into structured plans.

labs.name: Nous Research
labs.description: An independent research collective rather than a venture-backed lab. Hermes Agent became one of the most-downloaded open agentic models of 2025-2026. The vibe is craftsmanship: small team, high-quality fine-tunes, models that feel hand-tuned rather than mass-produced. Nous Hermes runs on Hostinger VPS budgets and powers the indie-builder agentic ecosystem.

models.name: Hermes 4
models.blurb: Open-weights agent model with native memory architecture. Free to download and run, popular with the $5/month-VPS builder ecosystem. Compounding intelligence as it accumulates skills.

models.name: Hermes Vision 2
models.blurb: Open-weights multimodal variant. Stronger than most open vision models on chart and screenshot understanding. Common pairing with Hermes for agent screen-reading workflows.
